topic: How many countries share the Nile basin? (11)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

britannica_nile.title: Nile River
britannica_nile.notes: basin spans Egypt, Sudan, South Sudan, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, DR Congo, Burundi, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania; length about 4,132 mi (6,650 km); White Nile from Lake Victoria and Blue Nile from Lake Tana converge at Khartoum

wiki_nile.title: Nile
wiki_nile.notes: drainage basin extends across eleven countries (list); basin ≈ 2,927,843 km² — about 10% of the African continent; South Sudan became the eleventh basin country in 2011

infonile_basin.title: The Nile Basin
infonile_basin.notes: basin = 10.3% of the continent, spreads over eleven countries (list); White Nile sources on the Equatorial Lake Plateau, Blue Nile in the Ethiopian highlands

conversation_nile.title: Why the 11 countries that rely on the Nile need to reach a river deal soon
conversation_nile.notes: more than 300 million people rely on the waters of the Nile; basin contains over 10% of Africa's landmass in 11 countries

claims.text: Eleven countries lie wholly or partly in the Nile basin: Burundi, DR Congo, Egypt, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania and Uganda.
vo: how many countries share the nile basin

claims.text: The river system runs from Lake Victoria (White Nile outlet at Jinja) north to the Mediterranean Sea.
The Nile is about 6,650 km (4,132 mi) long — the longest river in Africa (Britannica calls it the longest in the world; the Amazon claim is contested, so the script says 'in Africa').
vo: about six thousand six hundred and fifty kilometres

claims.text: The White Nile (from the Equatorial lakes) and the Blue Nile (from Lake Tana, Ethiopia) converge at Khartoum, Sudan.

claims.text: The basin covers roughly a tenth of Africa (Wikipedia ≈ 2.93 million km² ≈ 10%; InfoNile 10.3%; Britannica drains ≈ 3,349,000 km²).

myths.myth: The Nile flows through only Egypt and Sudan.
myths.reality: Its basin spans eleven countries; most of the water comes from the upstream states.
